f10_callout: What the value-parts percentage is, and is not: it is Best Value Parts proxy euro divided by value-parts plus contested-original proxy euro within the selected assortment, where each line's proxy euro is its reported quantity valued at the median CY2025 ISZE-to-distributor unit price for that part number. It is a proxy-euro mix measure inside the parts we sold — not a quantity share, not a share of expected service demand, and not a share of the market. The contested / original-only split is the older classification and has not yet been reconciled with the functional family plus market-attribute approach, so it is shown as a classification basis rather than as verified competitive exposure.Scope: Sales-to-dealer files for the listed distributors only — distributor stocking, not final customer demand. ITUK ≠ IUK. UTI ≠ UMI. Portugal is included as provisional coverage where the long file exists; it is not part of the controlled five-distributor dealer-level set.Second layer (distributor to dealer) CY2025. Networks: ITUK, UTI, IRELAND, IUK, GREECE, PORTUGAL. UTI is CV trucks. IUK is LCV pickups — Best Value Parts proxy-value share vs UTI is a tendency, not like-for-like trucks. ITUK dealer×PN SSOT plus Duncan network companion (PN×month thru Aug 2026, Customer Name=All). IUK ≠ ITUK; IRELAND ≠ IUK. AIM buckets: bvp | genuine_contested | genuine_only.Sales to dealer reports are quantity only — no dealer EUR. ISZE-denominated value = reported qty × median CY2025 ISZE to distributor unit price per PN (proxy for mix; not sales to dealer revenue). IUK is qty-only by design (no EUR chase). Part numbers with no billing price are reported as unvalued quantity and are never valued at zero inside the proxy totals. The euro figure is a known-price proxy; the unvalued quantity and its coverage are stated separately. Billing rows use actual invoice EUR and GPS.
